# Results — Study 712 ("CGC-graded key comics are an asset class")

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Do old comics beat the S&P? We
test the strongest tradable version of the graded-comic-as-investment claim: a graded-key-
comic **price index** (hardcoded, cited, **approximate** — a labelled proxy, not a live
feed) and the only *listed* thing even adjacent to the trade (Funko `FNKO`), each
benchmarked against `SPY`. Offline & deterministic; run `python examples/verify.py` to
reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Comic index | **Hardcoded, cited, approximate** annual graded-key-comic level (base 100 @ 2018-12-31), reconstructed from public GoCollect / Heritage reporting — see [`docs/references.md`](references.md). **A PROXY, not a feed.** |
| Equity proxy | `FNKO` (Funko, Nasdaq) — month-end Adj Close via yfinance, cached under `_cache/`. The *only* listed proxy — a poor one — because CGC/PSA parents and Heritage are private/delisted. |
| Benchmark | `SPY` (month-end Adj Close, yfinance) |
| As-of | 2025-12-31 (month-end; no partial-year bar) |
| Equity window | 2017-12 → 2025-12 (FNKO from its 2017-11 IPO; 96 monthly returns) |

> **Why a proxy, stated as a decision.** Real graded-comic indices (the GoCollect
> indices) are **paywalled**, and Heritage publishes per-lot archives rather than a
> downloadable index. Rather than fabricate a live tape we (a) hardcode a small,
> clearly-cited, **approximate** annual series whose *shape* — a 2020–21 pandemic melt-up,
> an **early-2022** blow-off top, a 2022–23 softening and a 2024–25 blue-chip
> stabilisation — is the load-bearing public fact, and (b) test the one **listed** proxy a
> public investor can actually buy. A toy company's equity is **not** the resale price of a
> CGC 9.8 key; it is a labelled proxy throughout, and the honest headline is that the trade
> has essentially **no** clean listed expression.

## Half 1 — did the comics beat the S&P? (comic index vs SPY)

The (approximate, cited) graded-key-comic index, year-end levels base 100:

| year | 2018 | 2019 | 2020 | 2021 | 2022 | 2023 | 2024 | 2025 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| level | 100 | 108 | 130 | **175** | 158 | 145 | 150 | 152 |
| YoY | — | +8.0% | +20.4% | **+34.6%** | −9.7% | −8.2% | +3.4% | +1.3% |

The reported **blow-off top was early 2022** (≈ level 188 on this scale); from there to
the 2024 low the index **round-tripped −20.2%**. Headline risk/return vs SPY:

| series | CAGR | ann. vol | Sharpe | max drawdown |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Graded-comic index** | **+6.16%** | 15.8% | 0.45 | **−17.1%** |
| SPY (year-end) | **+17.18%** | 16.9% | — | −18.2% |

**The comics lost the race outright:** ~6%/yr vs ~17%/yr for the S&P. The mean annual
excess (index − SPY) is **−11.3%/yr**, **t = −1.79** (p = 0.12, n = 7 years) — i.e. it
underperformed, but with only 7 annual observations the gap doesn't clear \|*t*\| ≥ 2 in
*either* direction; the honest read is "no evidence comics beat stocks, and the point
estimate is a large negative."

## Half 2 — the one tradable proxy vs SPY (all there is to buy)

Monthly Adj Close, Newey-West (6-lag) alpha vs SPY. **This is a labelled — and poor —
proxy**, used only because CGC/PSA parents and Heritage are private/delisted.

| series | CAGR | ann. vol | Sharpe | max DD | alpha/yr | beta | NW *t*(α) | p |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **FNKO** (Funko) | **−8.04%** | **66.9%** | 0.24 | **−88.1%** | −5.1% | 1.44 | −0.18 | 0.86 |
| SPY | +14.21% | 16.5% | **0.89** | −23.9% | — | — | — | — |

Funko shows **no significant alpha** vs SPY (\|t\| < 1) and a **negative** CAGR: it did the
collectibles bubble *with leverage*, falling **−88%** peak-to-trough. (Its Sharpe reads a
hair positive only because ~67% annual vol lifts the *arithmetic* mean while the
*geometric* return you keep is negative — pure volatility drag.) **No harvestable alpha,
and worse than SPY on every axis that matters.**

## Half 3 — the grading-fee + dealer-spread haircut (what flipping really costs)

The pitch never charges the friction. A buy-high / sell-into-an-auction-premium round trip
costs ~**25%** (buyer's premium + seller's commission, or a dealer buy/sell margin),
amortised over a ~**3-year** hold; plus a one-time ~**2%** CGC grading/slabbing fee (flat
on cheap books, a % of value on expensive keys); plus ~**1%/yr** insurance/storage. Charged
once on the index's gross CAGR:

| | value |
|---|--:|
| gross CAGR (index) | +6.16%/yr |
| − dealer/auction-spread drag (25% over 3y) | −9.14%/yr |
| − CGC grading fee (2% over 3y) | −0.67%/yr |
| − insurance/storage carry | −1.00%/yr |
| **= NET CAGR a real flipper earns** | **−5.15%/yr** |

The 6.2% gross *that already lost to the S&P* turns sharply **negative** once you pay CGC
to grade it and the dealer/auction house to move it. T-bills beat it; the S&P laps it.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is faithful

A deterministic, fixed-seed "bubble-and-round-trip" path (planted boom CAGR +55%, bust
−30%, σ = 5%/mo, seed 712): the inference engine recovers the planted up-sign and a finite
Sharpe — peak ≈ 460 → end ≈ 135, recovered CAGR **+5.19%**, Sharpe 0.34, max DD −70.7%,
`sign_ok = 1`. The harness can bank a planted signal, so a null on the real proxy is a real
null, not a broken pipeline.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE (it *under*-performs).** Over 2018–2025 the comic index returned
  ~6%/yr vs ~17%/yr for SPY; the annual excess is **−11.3%/yr (t = −1.79)** — no evidence
  comics beat stocks, and the point estimate is sharply negative. The one listed proxy
  shows **no significant alpha** (\|t\| < 1) *and* a losing CAGR. The "CGC comics are an
  asset class that beats the S&P" claim fails on the tape it's quoted on.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Even the gross index CAGR (6.2%) goes **negative (−5.2%/yr)**
  after a realistic CGC-grading + dealer-spread + carry haircut; the only listed proxy is a
  money-losing, 88%-drawdown wreck. Illiquid, high-carry, and a bubble that round-tripped
  2022–2024 in the speculative middle.
- **"Comics beat the S&P?" — BUSTED.** On return, risk-adjusted return, drawdown *and*
  net-of-cost, the S&P wins every column. The few who "made money" bought a specific key
  before 2021 and sold near the top — survivors of a bubble, not an asset class.

> **Caveat (named, not buried).** The comic index here is a **small, hardcoded,
> approximate** reconstruction of public reporting — its *level path/shape* is defensible
> but its precise year-end values are not a live feed, and the annual *t* rests on just 7
> observations. The equity proxy is exactly that — a *poor* proxy for "owning the comic
> trade," used because no clean listed vehicle exists. Both limitations push the verdict
> toward humility, not toward a stronger claim: nothing here says comics beat stocks, and
> several lines say the opposite.
